finalReport.rawFindings:
--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[CDN-1] Large static media in public/ served raw
File: public/video.mp4 (L1-L1)
Evidence: The public/ tree contains many high-resolution images and large media (e.g., public/video.mp4, public/wpvideo.mp4, multiple .JPG/.HEIC under "public/perle images", public/images/*.mp4/.webm). next.config.ts has no assetPrefix or global CDN domain for static/public assets and only documents next/image/loader behavior. 
Impact: High concurrent requests for these videos/images will drive large origin egress and exhaust server bandwidth/connection limits. 
Fix: Move large media to a CDN-backed origin (Cloudflare Images or R2 behind a CDN), remove heavy files from public, and serve via CDN domain with proper caching and streaming.

[CDN-2] Catalog/product APIs have no edge caching
File: src/app/api/products/route.ts (L1-L1)
Evidence: The repo exposes multiple high-traffic product/catalog API routes but I only found Cache-Control headers set on the cart endpoint; middleware and next.config.ts do not set s-maxage/stale-while-revalidate for catalog APIs.
Impact: Product list/detail requests will repeatedly hit the origin and database under load, causing DB/CPU/egress exhaustion and poor latency at scale. 
Fix: Add explicit Cache-Control (s-maxage, stale-while-revalidate) on product/list/detail responses and enable CDN edge caching for those endpoints.

[CDN-3] No next/image usage — images likely unoptimized
File: src/lib/cloudflare-images.ts (L1-L40)
Evidence: A custom Cloudflare loader utility exists and next.config.ts mentions loader options, but repository search returned no imports/usages of next/image; image tags appear to rely on public URLs or Cloudflare/R2 links instead of Next’s optimized Image component.
Impact: Pages can deliver full-resolution images (no responsive resizing/format negotiation), massively increasing bandwidth and client load time under traffic. 
Fix: Consistently use next/image with the custom cloudflareImageLoader (or ensure every image URL points to Cloudflare Image variants) and generate responsive variants (WebP/AVIF) for critical views.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[CDN-4] R2 code returns direct public R2 URLs (no CDN guarantee)
File: src/lib/r2-utils.ts (L1-L120)
Evidence: uploadToR2 and listStorageItems build and return URLs using R2_PUBLIC_URL (e.g., `${R2_PUBLIC_URL}/${key}`) with no enforced CDN domain or cache-control shaping in the helper.
Impact: If R2_PUBLIC_URL is an r2.dev/gateway without CDN fronting, client traffic will hit the storage gateway and cause high egress and slower delivery; caching behavior will vary by deployment.
Fix: Ensure R2_PUBLIC_URL points to a CDN-fronted domain or emit CDN-friendly URLs and add Cache-Control headers for immutable assets.

[CDN-5] Static asset requests bypass middleware but lack enforced headers
File: src/middleware.ts (L1-L40)
Evidence: The middleware matcher explicitly skips _next and static file extensions and the middleware does not set cache headers for assets; next.config.ts also contains no headers() configuration for static TTLs.
Impact: Static assets could be served without consistent Cache-Control, resulting in poor CDN hit ratios or origin requests depending on hosting defaults. 
Fix: Configure next.config.ts headers() to set long immutable TTLs for /_next/static and public assets, or set assetPrefix to a CDN and ensure appropriate Cache-Control.

--- INFO ---

[CDN-6] Cloudflare Images upload flow present
File: src/app/api/admin/upload-image/route.ts
Evidence: Upload endpoint posts to Cloudflare Images (uploadImageBufferToCloudflare) and returns imagedelivery.net variant URLs, which can provide CDN/variant benefits for images.
